title: Boston prep-school group with Dan Gerould, imitating Hot Fives
summary: With Dan Gerould and friends he played by ear, modelling on Armstrong, Morton and Oliver records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: I was a little bit of a jazz musician. I was a little bit of a jazz musician. I was a little bit of a jazz musician.

No, I wasn't good enough then. I was just learning. We had a little group, I remember, in Boston, a few fellows I know, including Dan Gerald, who you know, who I was in prep school with. There was a trumpet player and piano player and Dan Gerald on drums and myself. How does Gerald spell his name? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And we used to play at the trumpet player's house. His name was Ted Fales. And I began to become more under New Orleans influence. I began to listen to the Hot Fives, Jelly Roll Morton, King Oliver, and that sort of thing. And we sort of tried to emulate that. Were the other fellows similarly impressed? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yes, I think so. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Was it Dan who aroused that interest or all of you spontaneously? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. I can't remember exactly, but we used to play records and talk about them and we decided that that was the best form of jazz. That's what we should try to do. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Do you remember any tunes that you used? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Oh. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Oh. We played many of the jazz standards, the jazz me blues and...

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Any records stand out in your mind? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. You mean that I heard? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Do you recall of that period? Yes, that you'd imitate for example. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Oh, yeah. Some of the...

Some of the Hot Five records I think we used as models. I can't remember exactly which ones. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Did you depend on written scores to get an idea of how the chords went? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. No. At that period, most of us were sort of unfamiliar with what chords were. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And we just faked it. I mean, you know, we played entirely by ear and did the best we could. And I guess we had a lot of fun, but most of it sounded awful.
G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Now you mentioned Jolly Roll and Louie. Do you remember any of the other recording leaders?
G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, some of those small groups were Johnny Dodds. Generally the New Orleans groups we were mainly impressed with.
